title: The star formation region Messier 17
caption: The star formation region Messier 17, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: M 17, Messier 17, Swan Nebula · constellation Sagittarius · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This picture shows the rose-colored star-forming region Messier 17, taken with the Wide Field Imager, a camera on the 2.2-meter MPG/ESO telescope at ESO's La Silla site in Chile.

It counts among the sharpest images of the entire nebula. Sharpness and coverage are hard to combine, because a wide view is needed to take in the whole cloud and reveal its full size while fine detail must hold across the landscape of gas clouds, dust and newborn stars.

Star-forming regions like Messier 17 are clouds of gas and dust in which new stars are taking shape. The young stars light up and sculpt the surrounding gas. The telescope recorded the scene through blue, visual and red filters plus one that isolates the light of hydrogen, the most common element in such clouds. The official caption offers few further details about the region.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (35.44 x 33.12 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 57 × 53 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and R filters with a hydrogen-alpha filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the nebula's rose color is much more vivid here than it would be by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

alt: A rose-colored nebula of gas clouds, dust and newborn stars.
